title: Modules
lede: ES module syntax — named/default/namespace imports, re-exports, aliasing, and static CommonJS require — resolved by a whole-program model rather than separate compilation units. The big divergence is architectural: the resolver merges the entry file plus every transitive import into one program before codegen, so there is no runtime module object, no live bindings, and no separate-compilation boundary. Namespace imports and import.meta.url are compile-time-only constructs, an import cycle is restricted to declarations, and dynamic import() is the one unimplemented row.

entries.name: export function / const/let/var / interface / type / enum
entries.statusRow: export function / const/let/var / interface / type / enum
entries.signature: export function f() { ... }; export const x = ...; export interface I { ... }
entries.description: The export modifier on any top-level declaration — function, const/let/var, interface, type alias, or enum. It is a declaration-level modifier and nothing more: the resolver consumes it entirely while building each file's export table, so codegen never sees an export node.

entries.name: import { a, b } from './relative/path'
entries.description: Named imports from a relative-path module — named imports only, relative paths only (`./`, `../`) with `.ts` auto-appended if omitted. Resolved at compile time against the importing file's own directory (not `cwd`), then merged into the single whole-program AST.
entries.snippet: import { add, mul, Point, Direction, squareOf } from './math'

entries.name: Circular imports
entries.signature: // a.ts imports b.ts; b.ts imports a.ts
entries.description: Two files may import from each other and call each other's exported functions. The cycle is resolved once into the merged program.
differences: Supported only for the declarations-only case — a file in an import cycle can't run arbitrary top-level side-effecting code

entries.name: Diamond-shaped import graphs
entries.signature: // a → b, a → c, b → d, c → d
entries.description: A file imported from multiple places is parsed once and merged once, memoized by absolute path, so a shared dependency in a diamond graph contributes its declarations and runs its top-level code exactly once.

entries.name: Imported (non-entry) files may run top-level side-effecting code
entries.statusRow: Imported (non-entry) files may run top-level side-effecting code
entries.signature: // setup.ts top-level console.log runs before its importer's
entries.description: An acyclic imported file's top-level statements run exactly once, in real dependency order, strictly before whatever imports it — no restriction to declarations-only. Diamond-shared dependencies still run exactly once via per-path memoization.
entries.snippet:
import { ready } from './side_effects_setup'

console.log("main: ready = " + ready())
differences: A file that genuinely participates in an import cycle keeps the declarations-only restriction (no bare executable top-level statements), and additionally requires a top-level `var`/`let`/`const` initializer to be a compile-time literal — no TDZ/live-binding modeling

entries.name: True per-file module scope (mangled internal names)
entries.statusRow: True per-file module scope (mangled internal names)
entries.signature: // two files may both declare a top-level `helper`
entries.description: Every top-level declaration gets a file-private mangled name, and every reference to it is rewritten via a real scope-aware walk, so two unrelated files may freely declare the same top-level name. Binding two different files' exports to the same local name in one importing file with no `as` is still rejected — a real conflict, same as real ES modules.
entries.snippet:
import { run as runA } from './scoping_a'
import { run as runB } from './scoping_b'

entries.name: Import aliasing (import { a as b })
entries.description: A direct consequence of the per-file rename mechanism: `b` is simply bound to the target's mangled name for `a`, with no separate rename step.
entries.snippet:
import { run as runA } from './scoping_a'
import { run as runB } from './scoping_b'

entries.name: export default
entries.signature: export default function foo() { ... }; export default 42
entries.description: Named (function/class/interface/type/enum) and anonymous function/class forms, plus an arbitrary expression (`export default 42`, wrapped as a synthetic const). Exposed only under the export key "default" — a named default export's own name stays usable for intra-file self-reference (recursion, etc.) but is not itself importable via `import { foo }`, matching real ES modules.

entries.name: import x from './path' (default import)
entries.signature: import x from './path'; import x, { a, b } from './path'
entries.description: Also combinable with a named list in one statement (`import x, { a, b } from './path'`). Sugar over the same specifier machinery as a named import — no separate resolver mechanism.

entries.name: import * as ns from '...' (namespace import)
entries.description: `ns.member` is rewritten directly to that member's mangled name during resolution. Only actually-exported members are reachable (`ns.privateHelper` is rejected, same visibility rule as a named import); `ns.default` reaches a default export the same way any other member does.
entries.snippet:
import * as greetLib from './greet'
console.log(greetLib.shout("hey"))
console.log(greetLib.default("there"))
differences: Compile-time-only — `ns` is never a runtime value, usable only as the object of a non-computed dotted access; assigning it to a variable, passing it as a value, or `ns["x"]` reaches codegen as a plain undefined reference rather than a dedicated error message

Type-position access (`let x: ns.SomeInterface`) and `new ns.SomeClass(...)` are not supported — the latter a pre-existing, namespace-independent restriction (`new` already only accepts a single bare identifier)

entries.name: Static CommonJS require('<literal>')
entries.signature: const x = require('m'); const { a, b } = require('m')
entries.description: Desugared to the equivalent ES import at parse time, so it resolves and dispatches identically to `import` and interoperates with `import` in the same file. `const x = require('m')` binds the namespace (whole module object); `const { a, b } = require('m')` is a named import; bare `require('m')` is side-effect-only.
entries.snippet:
const path = require('path')
const { basename, extname } = require('path')
differences: Top-level, string-literal specifier only. `const x = require('m')` binds the namespace (whole module object); `const { a, b: c } = require('m')` is a named import; bare `require('m')` is side-effect-only. A destructuring default/nested-pattern/rest on a require binding, or a dynamic `require(expr)` / a `require` nested in a function body (lazy loading), is a clean compile error — deferred to the runtime/lazy-loading capability

entries.name: Re-exports (export { x } from './other', export * from './other')
entries.description: Named re-export list (with `as` aliasing) and star re-export both work, including default re-export in either direction. `export *` never forwards a default, matching real ES modules. Chains of arbitrary depth resolve transitively. A re-export forwards a name to this file's importers only — it does not become a usable bare identifier inside the re-exporting file itself.
entries.snippet:
export { add } from './re_export_core'
export { mul as multiply } from './re_export_core'
export { default as greet } from './re_export_core'
differences: No namespace re-exports (`export * as ns from`) — parsed and explicitly rejected with a clear error rather than silently mis-parsed, no concrete use case yet
Re-exporting from a built-in module (`export { readFileSync } from 'fs'`) is an explicit, rejected scope cut, not an oversight

entries.name: Bare/package-style imports (import x from 'somepackage')
entries.description: A bare specifier resolves against `klain_modules/<name>/klain.json`'s "main" field, found by walking upward once from the entry file's own directory (not re-walked per importing file, unlike Node). A real built-in module name (`'fs'`/`'path'`/etc.) is always checked, and always wins, before any `klain_modules` lookup is attempted.
differences: klmpm is Stage 1 only — deliberately just the resolution half; no klmpm tool exists yet to fetch/version/lock a dependency, so a `klain_modules/<name>/` directory has to be hand-constructed today
npm/`node_modules` interop is a separate, unstarted, differently-scoped mechanism

entries.name: Dynamic import(...)
entries.description: Parses cleanly (recognized in expression position) and is explicitly rejected with a "not yet supported" error, rather than a generic parse failure. Real support is staged separately as a later capability — the whole-program AOT model means a target's top-level code would still run at startup regardless of whether the call site executes.

entries.name: import.meta.url
entries.description: Resolved entirely at compile time, per file, into a plain string literal (`"file://" + that file's own absolute path`, matching real Node/browser convention) — codegen never sees a real module metadata object.
differences: `import.meta.url` is the only supported member — bare `import.meta` or any other member (`import.meta.resolve`, etc.) is a clean parse-time error

entries.name: Import-gated built-in bindings (fs/path/os/querystring/assert/http/cluster/Memory)
entries.signature: import fs from 'fs'; import { readFileSync } from 'fs'; import test from 'node:test'
entries.description: `import fs from 'fs'`, `import * as fs from 'fs'`, and `import { readFileSync } from 'fs'` (including aliasing and combining a default with named specifiers in one statement) all bind through the same scope-aware machinery as a real file import; every Node-named builtin also resolves under the node: prefix. A local variable of the same name correctly shadows it; importing an unknown member is a clean, explicit rejection. Node-style built-ins require a default, namespace, or named import; process/console stay ambient by design.
entries.snippet: import { readFileSync, writeFileSync as wfs, existsSync, unlinkSync } from 'fs'
